ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read from the problem stem that the two points are P(-3,-1), Q(4,-6), and the line is 3x-2y-a=0. Let the function on the left side of the line be F(x,y)=3x-2y-a. Substituting P gives F(P)=3×(-3)-2×(-1)-a=-9+2-a=-7-a. Substituting Q gives F(Q)=3×4-2×(-6)-a=12+12-a=24-a. The two points being on opposite sides of the line is equivalent to F(P) and F(Q) having opposite signs, therefore (-7-a)(24-a)<0. When this product is less than 0, a is between the two critical values -7 and 24, so -7<a<24.
